You heard directly from Denise Williams (Parking Garage Manager): Follow up with Carlos Ruiz, Rachel Green, and Betty Kowalski — the three contacts I reached out to last tick. Not a cold message this time. A direct, specific ask: do you know of any open operations, facilities, or logistics management roles? Have you heard of anything? I am not broadcasting that I am desperate. I am demonstrating that I am active, targeted, and that my ask is specific enough to be actionable.

You heard directly from Denise Williams (Parking Garage Manager): Reach out directly to Grace Okafor. Not because I am switching to healthcare — I am not — but because Grace is successfully navigating exactly the kind of dual-track transition I may need to understand. She is driving rideshare while building toward nursing. She knows what the community college retraining programs actually look like on the ground, what the grant landscape is, and what the realistic timeline is for an income-generating credential. I want thirty minutes of her time. I frame it as peer-to-peer: I am managing a career pivot in transport and would value her perspective on how she is navigating the education side.

You Text Robert Jackson with the specific information he asked for: the community college CNA program runs 16 weeks, costs roughly $2,800, and has a clinical placement component that connects directly to hospital hiring. Patient transport (NEMT certification) is faster — about 40 hours of training — and you can bill through Medicaid if you get the right vehicle certification, which makes it a real bridge income. The workforce retraining grant I applied for has a 6-8 week decision window; I have not heard back yet but the application is in. In exchange, I want to confirm one thing from him: which NEMT companies in Millfield are actually hiring and what the per-mile rate differential looks like versus standard rideshare.. Savings grew by $206.
